event.title: Indonesian Ferry KMP Mutiara Sentosa 2 Fire off Madura Island
event.summary: On Sunday, August 2, 2026, the Indonesian ferry KMP Mutiara Sentosa 2 caught fire at sea while sailing from Surabaya, East Java, to Makassar, South Sulawesi. At least five people were killed and 41 remained missing, while 225 were rescued, with rescue operations ongoing.

entities.relevance_to_event: The specific vessel that caught fire on August 2, 2026, carrying approximately 250 passengers and crew from Surabaya to Makassar.
The geographic location off which the ferry fire occurred while sailing in Indonesian waters.
The departure port of the KMP Mutiara Sentosa 2 and home to the Surabaya Search and Rescue Agency that coordinated the emergency response.
The intended destination of the ferry at the time the fire broke out during its voyage.
Location of a separate ferry sinking in July 2026 that demonstrated a pattern of recent maritime disasters in the region preceding this incident.
Ministry of Transportation official quoted as providing preliminary field reports on the evacuation status of passengers awaiting rescue by nearby vessels.
The Surabaya Search and Rescue Agency regional office that served as the primary official source for casualty figures and coordinated rescue operations, reporting 225 rescued, 5 dead, and 41 missing.
Government agency responsible for maritime safety and preliminary investigation into the cause of the fire.

claims.text: An Indonesian ferry caught fire at sea on August 2, 2026, off Madura Island.
claims.rationale: All five outlets across the left, center-left, and center-right spectrum report the same core event, satisfying cross-spectrum agreement.

framing_variants.characterization: Described as 'ferry catches fire off Indonesia' in a headline-style summary.
Reported as 'An Indonesian ferry caught fire at sea on Sunday.'
Stated as 'An Indonesian ferry caught fire at sea on Aug 2.'
Described as a fire off Madura Island 'on Sunday morning.'
BBC reports the fire occurred 'off Madura island.'

claims.text: The ferry involved in the fire is named KMP Mutiara Sentosa 2.
claims.rationale: Two outlets — Times of India (center-right) and BBC News (center-left) — both identify the vessel by name, though the other three articles do not mention it by name.

framing_variants.characterization: Identified as 'KMP Mutiara Sentosa 2' with the route from Tanjung Perak Port, Surabaya.
BBC identifies the vessel as 'passenger ship KMP Mutiara Sentosa 2.'

claims.text: Five people were killed in the ferry fire.
claims.rationale: All five outlets across left, center-left, and center-right report the same death toll of five, satisfying cross-spectrum agreement.

framing_variants.characterization: Al Jazeera reported 'At least five dead.'
South China Morning Post reported 'killing five people.'
The Straits Times reported 'killing five people.'
Times of India reported 'At least five people have died.'
BBC reported 'Five people have been found dead.'

claims.text: 41 people were missing following the ferry fire.
claims.rationale: All five outlets across the political spectrum report the identical figure of 41 missing persons.

framing_variants.characterization: Al Jazeera: '41 missing.'
SCMP: 'leaving another 41 missing.'
Straits Times: 'leaving another 41 missing.'
Times of India: '41 others remain missing.'
BBC: '41 are missing.'

claims.text: The ferry was carrying approximately 250 passengers and crew.
claims.rationale: Both BBC News (center-left) and Times of India (center-right) report approximately 250 people on board, satisfying cross-spectrum agreement.

framing_variants.characterization: Times of India reported 'around 250 passengers and crew.'
BBC reported 'carrying at least 250 people.'

claims.text: 225 people from the vessel were rescued.
claims.rationale: South China Morning Post and The Straits Times both report the rescue figure of 225, attributed to the Surabaya Search and Rescue Agency, but these two outlets are both center-left/center-right without left-leaning confirmation.

framing_variants.characterization: SCMP: 'A total of 225 people on the vessel were rescued,' citing the Surabaya Search and Rescue Agency.
Straits Times: 'A total of 225 people on the vessel were rescued,' with figures from an afternoon update by the agency.

claims.text: The ferry was sailing from Surabaya in East Java to Makassar in South Sulawesi when the fire occurred.
claims.rationale: Four outlets spanning left-leaning to center-right all confirm the same route, providing cross-spectrum agreement.

framing_variants.characterization: SCMP: 'sailed from Surabaya in East Java to Makassar in South Sulawesi.'
Straits Times used identical language.
Times of India: 'en route from Tanjung Perak Port in Surabaya to Makassar on Sulawesi Island.'
BBC: 'sailed from the country's second-largest city, Surabaya in East Java, to Makassar in South Sulawesi.'

claims.text: The ferry was located approximately 19 nautical miles north of Sapudi Island at the time of the incident.
claims.rationale: Only the Times of India provides the specific location of 19 nautical miles north of Sapudi Island, attributed to the Surabaya Search and Rescue Office.

framing_variants.characterization: Times of India: 'The Surabaya Search and Rescue Office said the ferry was located about 19 nautical miles north of Sapudi Island.'

claims.text: The captain reported the fire to authorities and subsequently lost contact with rescue officials.
claims.rationale: Four outlets spanning center-left and center-right confirm that the captain reported the fire and then went out of contact, with cross-spectrum sources agreeing.

framing_variants.characterization: SCMP: captain called the ferry company to report the fire and 'had not been in contact since then.'
Straits Times: captain 'had not been in contact with rescue officials after reporting the fire.'
Times of India: 'Communication with the vessel was lost shortly after, officials said.'
BBC: 'The captain of the ship reported the fire to Basarnas.'

claims.text: The Surabaya Search and Rescue office received notification that the ferry was on fire at 08:24 local time (02:24 GMT).
claims.rationale: Only BBC News provides the precise time at which the Surabaya Search and Rescue office was notified.

framing_variants.characterization: BBC: 'at 08:24 (02:24 GMT) the Surabaya Search and Rescue office received information that passenger ship KMP Mutiara Sentosa 2 was on fire.'

claims.text: According to the shipping company, the fire occurred at around 06:00–07:00 local time (00:00–01:00 GMT).
claims.rationale: Only BBC News reports the shipping company's estimated time of the fire's onset.

framing_variants.characterization: BBC: 'the fire occurred at around 06:00-07:00 (00:00-01:00 GMT)' per the shipping company.

claims.text: The ferry was almost entirely engulfed in flames.
claims.rationale: Both Times of India (center-right) and BBC News (center-left) report the ferry was nearly completely engulfed in flames, providing cross-spectrum corroboration.

framing_variants.characterization: Times of India: 'The vessel was almost completely engulfed in flames.'
BBC: the ferry 'was almost entirely engulfed in flames,' quoting Basarnas.

claims.text: Some passengers jumped into the sea and were picked up by a nearby ship; others gathered on the bridge and bow awaiting evacuation.
claims.rationale: Four outlets across center-left and center-right describe passengers jumping overboard and others waiting on the bridge and bow, with cross-spectrum agreement.

framing_variants.characterization: SCMP: 'Some passengers jumped into the sea and were picked up by a nearby ship.'
Straits Times: 'some jumped overboard' and were 'picked up by a nearby ship.'

Times of India: passengers in life jackets were gathered on one side, 'some are seen on video jumping of the vessel into the water'; others 'remaining on the bridge and at the bow awaiting evacuation.'
BBC: 'passengers held on in the ship's bridge and bow while awaiting rescue.'

claims.text: Four vessels were on standby near the ferry but could not approach due to the risk posed by flammable material on board.
claims.rationale: Three outlets — SCMP, Straits Times, and Times of India — all report four standby vessels unable to approach due to flammable material risk, though all are in the center-left to center-right range.

framing_variants.characterization: SCMP: 'Four other vessels were on standby near the ferry' but 'could not approach because of the risk posed by flammable material on the ferry.'
Straits Times: identical description of four standby vessels unable to approach due to flammable material.
Times of India: 'Four vessels are now alongside the ferry' while identifying specific rescue vessels TB Hasnur 26 and British Mentor assisting jumping passengers.

claims.text: The rescue vessel SAR 249 Permadi was en route to the scene from Surabaya, facing a journey of approximately six hours.
claims.rationale: Both Straits Times and Times of India report the six-hour travel time for additional rescue resources from Surabaya, with the Times of India identifying the vessel as SAR 249 Permadi.

framing_variants.characterization: Straits Times: 'A larger rescue operation was heading to the site from Surabaya' requiring 'a six-hour journey.'
Times of India: 'A rescue vessel, SAR 249 Permadi, was en route to the scene but faced an estimated travel time of about six hours.'

claims.text: Videos circulating on social media showed thick black smoke billowing from the upper decks and flames spreading through the ferry.
claims.rationale: Only the Times of India specifically references social media videos showing the fire's visual extent.

framing_variants.characterization: Times of India: 'Videos circulating on social media showed thick black smoke billowing from the upper decks as flames spread through the ferry.'

claims.text: The cause of the fire was unknown and remained under investigation at the time of reporting.
claims.rationale: Both Times of India (center-right) and BBC News (center-left) explicitly state the fire's cause was unknown and under investigation, providing cross-spectrum agreement.

framing_variants.characterization: Times of India: 'the cause of the fire remains under investigation.'
BBC: 'It was unclear how the ferry caught fire.'

claims.text: Ministry of Transportation official Muhammad Masyhud stated that, based on preliminary field reports, passengers were waiting to be evacuated by nearby vessels.
claims.rationale: Only The Straits Times names and quotes Ministry of Transportation official Muhammad Masyhud on the status of passengers.

framing_variants.characterization: Straits Times: Muhammad Masyhud, a senior official at the Ministry of Transportation, said 'passengers are waiting to be evacuated by the vessels in the vicinity of the incident site' based on preliminary field reports.

claims.text: In July 2026, a separate ferry carrying over 70 people sank near Selayar island south of Sulawesi; four people were found dead and 14 remained missing by the end of the search operation.
claims.rationale: Only The Straits Times references the prior July 2026 ferry sinking near Selayar island as context for Indonesia's maritime safety record.

framing_variants.characterization: Straits Times contextualized the August incident by noting a July ferry sinking near Selayar that killed four and left 14 missing.

background.point: Indonesia is an archipelago nation heavily reliant on ferry transport across its thousands of islands, and has a history of maritime accidents due to overcrowding, aging vessels, and adverse sea conditions.
The Surabaya Search and Rescue Agency (Basarnas regional office) served as the primary official source for casualty and rescue figures in this incident.

In July 2026, just weeks before this incident, another Indonesian ferry sank near Selayar island south of Sulawesi, killing four and leaving 14 missing — illustrating a pattern of recent maritime disasters in the region.
Surabaya is Indonesia's second-largest city and home to the Tanjung Perak Port, a major hub for inter-island ferry services.

paragraphs.text: An Indonesian ferry caught fire at sea on August 2, 2026, off Madura Island while sailing from Surabaya in East Java to Makassar in South Sulawesi. The vessel, identified by some sources as KMP Mutiara Sentosa 2, was carrying approximately 250 passengers and crew when the incident occurred.

At least five people were killed in the fire, and 41 remained missing as of the time of reporting. Rescue operations successfully evacuated 225 people from the vessel, according to the Surabaya Search and Rescue Agency.

The ferry was almost entirely engulfed in flames during the incident. Some passengers jumped into the sea and were picked up by a nearby ship, while others gathered on the bridge and bow awaiting evacuation.

The captain reported the fire to authorities and subsequently lost contact with rescue officials. Four vessels were on standby near the ferry but could not approach due to the risk posed by flammable material on board.
The cause of the fire remained unknown and under investigation at the time of reporting, with authorities conducting preliminary inquiries into the incident.

Indonesia's maritime safety record has been under scrutiny following multiple ferry incidents. In July 2026, a separate ferry carrying over 70 people sank near Selayar island south of Sulawesi, resulting in four deaths and 14 people remaining missing by the end of the search operation.

Center-right outlets reported the ferry was located approximately 19 nautical miles north of Sapudi Island at the time of the incident, according to the Surabaya Search and Rescue Office. This specific geographic detail appeared only in coverage from The Times of India.

Center-left outlets provided different timing details for the emergency response. BBC News reported that the Surabaya Search and Rescue office received notification of the fire at 08:24 local time (02:24 GMT), though the shipping company estimated the fire had begun earlier, around 06:00–07:00 local time (00:00–01:00 GMT).

Center-right sources reported that videos circulating on social media showed thick black smoke billowing from the upper decks and flames spreading through the ferry, providing visual documentation of the fire's severity.

The Straits Times, a center-right Singaporean outlet, quoted Ministry of Transportation official Muhammad Masyhud, who stated that based on preliminary field reports, passengers were waiting to be evacuated by nearby vessels. This official account of the evacuation status was not reported by other outlets in the source set.

Additional rescue resources faced significant travel time to reach the scene. The rescue vessel SAR 249 Permadi was en route from Surabaya, facing a journey of approximately six hours to arrive at the location of the stricken ferry.
